decisions.reason: This organic sliced ham fits the firm's stated plan to expand organic lines and costs little to keep on existing slicing lines, so the option is still worth holding while the lack of post-2019 evidence leaves its value unresolved.
This organic Kasseler is a cheap extension of an established self-service format in line with the organic strategy, and there is no evidence that its value has failed.
This organic pepper salami uses existing maturation facilities at low marginal cost and supports the organic range expansion, so keeping the option open is justified.

The exotic teriyaki aspic is a riskier niche item for the service counter, where shelf space is shrinking, but small-batch counter production keeps its carrying cost moderate, so it stays for now with a high risk of being dropped.
This fennel salami got a page of its own, signalling commitment, and as a close variant of the established salami range it is cheap to maintain.
This classic liver pâté with veal sits squarely in the firm's core pâté competence with low carrying cost and steady traditional demand, so dropping it is not warranted.
